Avenda adds Surgery Mode to bring Unfold AI maps into prostate procedures

The update aligns views with surgical cameras and adds intraoperative MRI review as physician decision support, not autonomous surgery.

The Robot Report ↗20 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

From planning into the operating room

Avenda Health introduced Surgery Mode on October 20 to use Unfold AI’s prostate cancer estimation maps during procedures, including robot-assisted surgery. It extends support beyond preoperative consultation and planning. The technology assists physicians in reviewing information rather than making decisions or performing surgery autonomously.

Patient-specific maps and camera alignment

Unfold AI combines MRI, biopsy, pathology and PSA information into a patient-specific 3D map. The new mode enlarges views, adjusts map orientation including left-right alignment to the surgical camera, enables review of underlying MRI slices during the procedure and exposes Capsule Risk Score within a surgical view.

Workflow updates alongside visualization

The update also improves case visibility through patient lists, filters, notes and assigned-physician information for team coordination. This is a software capability announcement, not evidence that use of the new mode has already demonstrated lower recurrence or superior treatment outcomes.
